purpose: Structural rules and calendar of the 2004 NBA playoffs, researched October 2026. Rules and dates only: no real 2004 seeds, matchups or results are recorded here or used by the simulation.

status_values.derived: inferred from cited sources, reasoning given
status_values.design_choice: not verifiable for 2003-04; the simulation's documented choice

divisions.note: Last season with two divisions per conference; six divisions from 2004-05.

qualification.seeding: The two division winners take seeds 1 and 2, ordered by record; seeds 3 to 8 are the next six records in the conference.
qualification.quote: Prior to 2004, when the NBA was aligned into two conferences with two divisions each, the division champions were guaranteed the top two seeds.

bracket.note: The fixed bracket used 1984-2004: winners of 1-8 and 4-5 meet; winners of 3-6 and 2-7 meet; no reseeding.

series.note: The first round became best-of-seven in 2003.

home_court.who: the better regular-season record; equal records by the tiebreak procedure
home_court.who_status: sourced for the Finals (better record); design_choice for the conference rounds, where 2003-04 seed versus record is unverified (record is used, as from 2004-05)

tiebreakers.basis: The long-standing NBA order as NBA.com publishes it, with the pre-2016 rule that division winner applies in a two-team tie only after head-to-head; the exact 2003-04 wording could not be read from an archive.
tiebreakers.restart: Once a team is separated, the remaining tied teams start the procedure again (two-team or multi-team).
tiebreakers.drawing: an engine decision draw, journaled like any other, so it cannot be chosen or re-rolled

calendar.status: sourced for the opening days; derived for the gap template (matchups and television set the real days)

first_round.note: Four series open each day, each conference two and two (sourced); which pairs open which day is a design choice. Gaps G1-G2 and G2-G3 of three days, then every other day (derived).

conference_semifinals.note: Game 1 on the conference's opening day or two days after both feeding series end, whichever is later (derived).

finals.note: Games 1-5 sourced; games 6 and 7 derived from the Sunday/Tuesday/Thursday pattern.
